text:
Simon Nemec was the second pick in the 2022 draft, the defenseman the Devils took right after Juraj Slafkovsky. New Jersey traded him to Calgary for picks, and the Flames gave him a five-year contract. Twenty-three games in, he is playing 21 minutes a night, and on Nov. 17 in San Jose he scored his first goal as a Flame, on the power play. The Calgary Herald has since asked what his ceiling is.

So far he has 2 goals and 7 assists, a points rate right at the league average for defensemen. He's 22, and he skates well: his top speed is in the 89th percentile in NHL Edge tracking.

The defensive results are the open question. Calgary gets 45% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on, 3.5 points worse than without him. But the Flames have also scored 3.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from his New Jersey season liked his blue line: he stopped 18% of entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman. That is the part of his game worth watching now.
headline: Settling in Calgary
